obligation: Utility incident notice: 27 addenda with a 24-hour term
citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 1 (contract term; flows down CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.1)
trigger: Company confirms a cyber incident related to the products or services it supplies to that utility (TMU firmware or configuration software, the code signing key or build pipeline, field laptops or field access to utility sites, FMS or STRS data for subscribers and members)
deadline: Within 24 hours after confirmation (contract deadline, not a NERC requirement)
notify: Each utility's designated security contact, by the method in its addendum (contacts in the obligations register and the printed incident binder)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual (27 of 88 addenda). The register and templates still use a single 48-hour clock until POAM-016 closes (2026-11-30); until then the case lead checks each addendum
verified: true (CIP-013-2 text on nerc.com); deadline is a contract term per scenario
clock_starts: Confirmation that the incident relates to products or services supplied (recorded by the incident commander)
owner: Chief Compliance Officer (sends after counsel review)

obligation: Utility incident notice: 61 addenda with a 48-hour term
citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 1 (contract term; flows down CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.1)
trigger: Same as the 24-hour row
deadline: Within 48 hours after confirmation (contract deadline, not a NERC requirement)
notify: Each utility's designated security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual (61 of 88 addenda, including 12 AQ-01 contracts not yet loaded in the register; POAM-016)
verified: true (CIP-013-2 text on nerc.com); deadline is a contract term per scenario
clock_starts: Confirmation that the incident relates to products or services supplied

citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 2 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.2 flow-down)
trigger: Any incident notified under sec. 1
deadline: Ongoing until closure: share indicators, affected firmware versions, and recovery steps for supplied products; join utility calls when asked
notify: Addendum utility security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual (all 88)
verified: true (CIP-013-2 text on nerc.com); deadline is a contract term per scenario
owner: Director of Product Security with the Chief Compliance Officer

citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 3 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.3 flow-down)
trigger: A company representative's remote or onsite access to a utility should no longer be granted (termination, role change, or credentials possibly exposed, for example field laptops encrypted or stolen in the incident)
deadline: Within 1 business day
notify: Each utility where the representative holds access
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual (all 88). 3 of 41 notices were late in 2026 (POAM-016)
verified: true (CIP-013-2 text on nerc.com); deadline is a contract term per scenario
clock_starts: Termination, role change, or the finding that credentials may be exposed
owner: Vice President, Spares and Services (field service)

citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 4 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.4 flow-down)
trigger: The investigation finds a vulnerability in supplied TMU firmware, the configuration software, or other supplied software
deadline: Within 30 days of the company knowing of it (internal escalation at day 20, POAM-019)
notify: Addendum utility security contacts; coordinated vulnerability disclosure advisory to all TMU customers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual (all 88). 1 of 9 disclosures in 2026 went out on day 38
verified: true (CIP-013-2 text on nerc.com); deadline is a contract term per scenario

obligation: Firmware integrity after a pipeline or signing key incident
citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 5 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.5 flow-down)
trigger: Build pipeline, code signing key, or download portal possibly compromised
deadline: With the sec. 1 notice: tell utilities which releases are trusted; revoke the key and re-sign releases with new hashes before any further download
notify: Addendum utility security contacts; all TMU customers through the download portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual (all 88)
verified: true (CIP-013-2 text on nerc.com); deadline is a contract term per scenario
clock_starts: Confirmation that the pipeline or key may be compromised

trigger: Confirmed unauthorized access to subscriber data, or an outage that affects condition advisories
deadline: Data incident: within 72 hours of confirmation. Outage: status notice when the 4-hour RTO will be missed; advisories for high-severity alerts within 24 hours by phone if the portal is down
notify: About 60 subscriber utilities (contract contacts)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. The FMS has no connection into utility networks, so a production ransomware event does not reach subscriber systems
clock_starts: Confirmation of the data incident; start of the outage

trigger: Confirmed unauthorized access to member data, or an outage of the STRS portal or spare registry
deadline: Data incident: within 72 hours of confirmation. Outage: immediately, with the manual dispatch line; the 24-hour dispatch decision commitment still applies
notify: 27 member utilities (contract contacts)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
clock_starts: Confirmation of the data incident; start of the outage

obligation: Delivery-impact and force majeure notices to customers
trigger: Production delay affecting committed deliveries, storm-restoration units, or liquidated damages milestones
deadline: Per each supply agreement (as soon as the delay is known; many agreements set a short written notice period for force majeure claims)
notify: Customer purchasing and project contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - business and contractual, not a legal reporting duty. Counsel decides whether to claim force majeure
owner: Chief Operating Officer with the General Counsel

citation: Federal contract terms; FAR 52.204-21 has no incident reporting paragraph
trigger: Incident delays deliveries under any of the 11 federal contracts or affects FCI
deadline: No cyber incident reporting duty under FAR 52.204-21. Notify the contracting officer of any delivery schedule impact under the contract terms (counsel confirms)
notify: Contracting officers for the 11 civilian contracts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 11 civilian federal contracts

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services identified
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment or services identified during response or rebuild (for example a replacement camera, router, or modem)
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (civilian agencies)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 11 federal contracts
clock_starts: Identification or notice from a subcontractor

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: A Kaspersky Lab covered article is identified in anything provided to the Government under the contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (civilian agencies)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 11 federal contracts
clock_starts: Identification or notice from a subcontractor

citation: FAR 52.204-30(c)(3)-(4); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: A covered article or source subject to a FASCSA order was provided to the Government or used in contract performance (for example replacement hardware bought during recovery)
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (civilian agencies)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the 8 contracts awarded since 2024
clock_starts: Identification or notice from a subcontractor

trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material (any severity-1 incident, including any production outage at a plant)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.5)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (employee, former employee, and applicant data from HR, payroll, and applicant tracking; definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (employees live mainly in FL, GA, TN, TX, NC, and OH); counsel's state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)
owner: Chief Human Resources Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (payroll, benefits, applicant tracking) has a breach
deadline: Varies by state
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts; 4 AQ-01 vendor contracts have no notice term (P03 G-153)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employees and former employees are mostly Florida residents)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b); 15 more days on written good cause under 501.171(3)(a))
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida residents are affected
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, content of notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not resulted in and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if that determination is made

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents' personal information

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As early as practical (target within 24 hours of declaration; supports OFAC mitigation and sector threat sharing)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-05. If finalized as proposed, the company would be covered under both the size criterion (exceeds the SBA size standard for NAICS 335311) and the critical manufacturing sector criterion (NAICS subsector 335). Report voluntarily now (P01 R-060)

trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: 72 hours
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: No - no DoD contracts or subcontracts; the bid review gate keeps it that way. Recorded for completeness

obligation: Form DOE-417 electric emergency incident and disturbance report
trigger: Cyber or physical events affecting electric system operations
deadline: Not applicable to the company
notify: DOE
applies_at_this_tier: No - the form applies to electric utilities and the other entities named in its instructions, not to equipment manufacturers. A utility customer may have to file if a supplied product affects its systems; the company supports it under addendum sec. 2
verified: true (Form DOE-417 and instructions, OMB 1901-0288, checked 2026-10-05)

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging any incident vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline (breach counsel, forensics, OT-capable response firm)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

deadline: Within 72 hours of the supplier confirming the incident (standard Tier 1 term)
notify: Director of Third-Party Risk Management (SOC case)
